3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Zaminder of Sree Faltani and to the waqf estate of Baliyadi Zaminder; that the then British government acquired the suit land measuring 125 acres including other land of this area for certain period for converting this area as government forest land by notification No. 1139 dated 14-11-1951 after serving notice upon the Zaminder and local people on 11-8-1951; that SA and RS khatian were correctly prepared in the names of the government and the forest department; that again, the suit land was permanently acquired by the government vide notification No. 4836 LR and No. 4849 LR dated 2-4-1956 and thus the suit land was permanently vested in the government and forest department annulling all the rights of the Zaminder therein and that the suit land has already been in the control and possession of the government as per notification No. XII / Forest 13-19 /85 /19 dated 31-3-1985 under section 4 of the Forest Act. It is further contended that the suit land has been entered into the Khatian of Forest Department; that the office of Divisional Forest Officer is located at Moakhali that there is no office of Forest Department at Kaliakore; that in order to suppress the summons, the address of the Divisional Forest Officer was shown at Kaliakore; that summons was not served upon the Divisional Forest Officer in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that suppressing the summons collusively and on practising fraud upon the Court, the defendants illegally obtained ex parte decree on 4-12-1975 and that the defendants in order to grab the forest land created some forged papers. It is further stated that the appearance of the Government pleader and filing of written statement was fraudulently shown; that the suit land was all along in the possession of Forest Department; that the defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land; that knowing about the ex prrte decree in title Suit No.329 of 1974 on 4-12-1975 from Misc. case No. 4 of 1968 of ADC (Rev), Gazipur, the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of the ex parte decree void and for declaration of title in respect of the suit land. 

 5. The case of the defendant Nos.1 to 6, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the khas possession of then Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkar Roy of Showapur, PS Dhamria whose interest was that of a tenure holder in respect of the suit property and his name was recorded as such in the CS khatian and in the relevant registers and that while having such tenure interest, the said Zaminder by an unregistered amalnama dated 15th Poush 1344 BS settled the suit land to Md Abdul Gafur, who took physical possession of the said land after obtaining such allotment and since then they have been possessing the land by annually selling the jungles to the buyers who took the same for cutting and taking away the shrubs and trees for use as fuel. It is further contended that Abdul Gafur died leaving 6 sons namely, Serajul Islam, Furat Ali, Abdul Balek, Noya Miah, Chanda Lai and Elihi Box; that the heirs of Abdul Gafur were also in possession of suit land; that Serajul Islam and the other heirs of Serajul Islam filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 against the Department of Forest for permanent injunction restraining them from disturbing their peaceful possession; that summons of that suit was properly served; that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement but lastly, he did not turn up and ultimately the suit was decreed ex parte on 4-12-1975. 

 12. On the other hand, the defendant No. 7 only contested the suit and filed Zamindari Pattannama, some Zamindari Dhakhilas, some government Dhakhilas, CS khatian and certified copies of SA khatians which have been exhibited under different marks. 

 17. He further submits that the suit property were vested absolutely in the hand of the Government as "forest land" by a gazette notification No. 1139 dated 14-11-51 after serving the notice upon the Zaminder on 11-8-1951 and the local people on 11-8-1951; that moreover, the SA khatian and RS khatian were correctly prepared in the name of the Government and the Forest Department; that the suit property cannot be settled by anyone to anybody; that the plaintiff of the present suit was not made party as defendant in the earlier title suit No. 329 of 1974; that the present defendant as plaintiffs collusively made wrong persons as defendants in that earlier suit and that managed false signatures in summons notice and collusively obtained fraudulent decree suppressing summons. He further submits that the plaintiff came to know about the ex parte decree of earlier suit after getting notice against the Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1988 in the Court of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) on 5-7-1988; that no pattan was given by Zaminder to Abdul Gafur and that the rent receipts and khatians were manufactured and that the finding and decision both are erroneous in law as well as on fact, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. 

 33. The learned Deputy Attorney-General stoutly submits that the amalnamas, Dakhalias and rent receipts are false and fabricated. In support of his contention, he firstly argues that the heirs of Abdul Gafur did contest the suit; that they have not been adduced as witness; that subsequent purchaser, defendant No. 7, Habibur Rahman, only deposed that he was not party in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that he cannot say how the plaintiff got the suit land and that the DW 1 is not a proper witness. His second submission is that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 have failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land and the plaintiff of that suit have not taken any step to contest the suit filed by the government. He lastly submits that the amalnama alleged to have been granted by Zaminder on the 15th Poush, 1344 BS corresponding to sometime in the year 1938 BS; that CS record was finally published in between 1919 and 1921; that CS record which was finally published long before 1938 AD and thus the appearance of the name of Abdul Gafur in CS Khatian, who alleged to have taken settlement some time in 1938 AD, have been proved to be fabricated and manufactured one. Moreover, the amalnama has not been proved as per law. 

 34. We find substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney-General. Since the foundation of Title of the defendants-respondents has not been proved and thus the CS khatian has been proved fabricated and manufactured and the SA khatian prepared on the basis of alleged CS khatian has no leg to stand. Dhakalias granted on the basis of khatian does not create any title which was also obtained fraudulently. 

 40. In the facts and circumstance of the case and evidence on record, we are inclined to hold that the defendants-respondents obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 suppressing summons collusively and practising fraud upon the Court. Again, the defendants-respondents manufacturing some false and concocted amalnama dhakhilas and khatians tried to validate the evil design of grabbing huge quantum of the forest khas land practising fraud upon the Court and their evil design has been revealed in the appeal. The essence of law being to advance the cause of justice and not to frustrate it. If fraud is allowed to be perpetratect and perpetuated the sanctity attached to law will wither away with disastrous consequences to the society. The case of the defendants-respondents is the glaring example of committing fraud upon the Court which cannot be encouraged.
